pages.title: The Energy Orbit — how ACT builds, measures, and protects relational energy
pages.excerpt: The orbit is everyone who brings ACT doing, energy, and life. We sort people by energy, not by what they pay. This doc is the practice: how we see the orbit, how we've grown it, how we keep it warm, and how we stop it leaking — so energy turns into projects that fund themselves, not a treadmill that burns the founders out.
pages.content:
> The orbit is everyone who brings ACT *doing, energy, and life*. [[relationship-first-crm|We sort people by energy, not by what they pay]]. This doc is the practice: how we see the orbit, how we've grown it, how we keep it warm, and how we stop it leaking — so energy turns into projects that fund themselves, not a treadmill that burns the founders out.

## The orbit, plainly

Picture ACT at the centre and the people around it in rings. The pull inward is not money — it is **reciprocal energy**: people we *do things with*, who bring life, who we'd call to build something. The inner ring is the **Getting Shit Done Alliance** ([[relationship-first-crm|`circle:gsd-alliance`]]) — hand-picked, never computed. As you move outward the relationships thin into the transactional: a cold connection request, a one-off ask, a newsletter open. **The transactional edge is fine and necessary. The work is keeping the centre relational, and making the centre also the place revenue comes from.**

Two lanes, never one funnel:
- **Supporter lane** — the rings above. Climbs by energy; this is what the orbit measures.
- **Community lane** — Oonchiumpa, storytellers, elders. A **parallel constellation**, co-owners held by consent and the [[ecosystem-value-exchange|OCAP-holds / CARE-owes]] frame. **Never ringed, never energy-scored, never in a drip.** Measuring community by "energy to ACT" is the exact extraction the whole model refuses.

## How we read it — the vibe pass

The "vibe pass" is a **metadata-only** sweep of the warm channels the email spine can't see — WhatsApp, iMessage, LinkedIn, Signal via Beeper. It reads *who / how often / how recently / how two-way*, **never message content**, and **only the supporter lane**. For each person:

- **Recency** — days since last exchange.
- **Frequency** — message volume (depth of contact).
- **Reciprocity** — the share you send vs receive. Balanced (~0.3–0.7) is a real two-way relationship; all-inbound is someone reaching toward you; all-outbound is you chasing.

These combine into a single orbit score (recency 40% · frequency 35% · two-way balance 25%) and a **pattern**:

| Pattern | Means | Energy reading |
|---|---|---|
| **generative** | reciprocal + active | energy *source* — the core |
| **inbound-lean** | they reach, you rarely reply | energy *asked of you* — gold or drain; needs a human read |
| **outbound-lean** | you chase, little back | energy *spent* — a one-sided pursuit |
| **cooling** | was deep, gone quiet | latent energy — worth re-warming |
| **light** | one or two touches | the transactional edge |

**Three honesty rules, or the number lies:**
1. **The score measures *channel intimacy*, not worth.** WhatsApp/iMessage score high because that's where real talk happens; LinkedIn scores low because it's a doorway, not a lounge. A low LinkedIn score (George Newhouse, Scott McDougall, Phoebe Frederick) means *"not our channel with them yet,"* not *"low value."*
2. **It's a prompt for judgement, not a verdict.** Energy can't be computed — the Alliance stays [[relationship-first-crm|hand-curated]]. The pass surfaces candidates; a human decides.
3. **It's one lens of three.** Beeper = informal channels. The [[#relates-to|Gmail spine]] = the two-way email network (264 people, funder-heavy). GHL = the system of record. The orbit is real only when all three are reconciled onto one person.

## What the first pass shows (snapshot, 2026-06-03 — Verified from Beeper metadata)

55 supporter-lane people scored: **24 generative, 4 inbound-lean, 27 light.** The shape proves the thesis:

- **The generative core lives on WhatsApp + iMessage. LinkedIn is almost entirely light or inbound.** Relational energy and the cold-outreach channel are physically different places.
- **The system can't see our warmest people.** Ben Croft scores 91 (reciprocal, recent, years deep) and **isn't in GHL at all** — he lives in WhatsApp, never promoted to a contact. The orbit's whole job is to surface the Ben Crofts.
- **The hottest live pod is Contained** — a cluster of iMessage threads all balanced and active *today*, bound by a thing being built together right now.
- **People are reaching in and we're not catching them.** Phoebe Frederick (NFP transparency map), Dr Terry Hutchinson (journal), Anurag Gummadi (Contained) sit in *light/inbound* — **latent energy**, real interest never reciprocated into relationship.
- **The one-sided signal is legible.** Peter Norden AO: 23 in / 3 out — a relationship doing work in one direction. Worth a human read, not an auto-anything.

*(Inferred, not verified: lane labels and the "latent/cold" reads are judgement on top of the metadata, for Ben to confirm. Family — e.g. Carla Knight — topped the raw score and is filtered out; the orbit is the network, not the household.)*

## How we've built energy — the evidence

The orbit didn't come from a CRM. It came from **shared doing**. The pattern repeats across every project:

- **Contained (JusticeHub)** — you don't pitch the youth-justice story, you put people *inside* it. The visceral shared experience makes champions, and the champions become the network. The current Adelaide / Victoria Square push is a working group of people who felt it together.
- **Community Capital / Caravan Collective retreat** — a few days together turned into durable bonds ("beautiful memories of a very special few days"). The *experience* was the relationship engine.
- **Goods on Country · Harvest · Witta** — building on the land with people. The garden crews, the "Witta Harvest Adventure" (a kid who "loved it, keen to come again") — place-based doing that bonds families, not transactions.
- **Empathy Ledger** — storytelling as the renewal mechanism: people show who they are, *really well, and they own it*. Energy flows back to the person; [[relationship-first-crm|case studies prove the venture]] for ACT. One engine, two outputs.
- **Snow Foundation** — proof that a funder relationship can be genuinely warm and aligned (easy banter, reconciled tranches). When alignment is real, **energy and revenue arrive together**.
- **Soleful crew / dreaming sessions** — peer energy with people like Ben Croft: Bali dreaming, the Greens event, "keep this dream rocking." No transaction, pure orbit.
- **Oonchiumpa** — the guardrail case. A deep partnership that must **never** be pulled toward an ACT-centred funnel; it is held as a sovereign constellation. Energy here is *mutual obligation*, not pull-toward-centre.

## How we keep building it — connected experiences

The future isn't more outreach. It's more *experiences that bond*, and a system that recognises them. Four mechanisms:

1. **Pods as first-class, not just individuals.** The bonding unit is the small group doing a thing — the Contained crew, the retreat, the garden crew, Soleful. The CRM should hold the *experience that bonded people*, not only the person (a `pod:` alongside `circle:gsd-alliance`).
2. **Storytelling as renewal.** People sharing their story in service of what they're passionate about refills energy *and* makes them feel **seen, not segmented**. Pointed inward at the network, not only outward at funders.
3. **Membership as mutual commitment, decoupled from money.** Support mechanisms and groups to help each other get what we all want — belonging you opt into, not a tier you buy.
4. **Peer support, not hub-and-spoke.** People supporting *each other*, so Ben and Nic aren't the only energy source. ACT convenes; it doesn't gatekeep from the centre.

## Where energy comes from — and where it's taken

The reason to map this at all: **protect the founders' energy and the revenue at the same time.** They are not in tension — misaligning them is the failure mode.

**Energy sources (invest here):**
- Generative-pattern people on the warm channels — the reciprocal core.
- Pods mid-build (Contained now) — shared momentum is renewable.
- Aligned funders (Snow) where the cheque *and* the relationship are real.
- Storytelling moments — they pay energy back.

**Energy drains (name them, don't absorb them):**
- **The philanthropy treadmill.** The email spine skews funder-heavy; the doers are buried. Chasing misaligned funders for survival drains energy and lets them set the agenda. Discipline: keep the misaligned *light and transactional* without guilt; don't let a grant become the identity ([[four-lanes|Grants is one lane of four]]).
- **Money stress as an energy tax.** Runway and overdue invoices are themselves a drain (the daily money brief is the canary). The answer is not "chase more grants" — it's making the **generative core the revenue core** through commercial pipelines that pay the founders ([[relationship-first-crm|Goods, Harvest — money as plumbing]]).
- **Inbound-lean asymmetry.** One-sided demand (the Peter Norden pattern). Triage it: convert the *aligned* ones to two-way (Phoebe, Terry, Anurag are latent gold), let the rest stay light. Not every inbound deserves your energy.
- **Community-as-management.** Spending energy "running" community through funnels is both extractive and exhausting. Releasing it into genuine partnership returns energy (fix the [[ecosystem-value-exchange|Kristy/Oonchiumpa drip violation]]).

**The maintenance loop:** run the vibe pass periodically → concentrate time on the generative-and-revenue-aligned → convert latent inbound that fits → keep community sovereign → let the cold edge stay cold. Energy in, sustainable projects out, more energy back.

## The operating loop this enables

The orbit is the read; the system is the loop. Sources → one orbit → a home + a tag for every real person → comms and visualisation that fit the ring → match people to what each project actually needs → bring the shown energy in. Detailed sequencing (tracer-first, GHL writes gated and human-in-loop) lives in the plan: **`thoughts/shared/plans/2026-06-03-act-network-circle-action-stages.md`**.

## Provenance
- Orbit numbers: Beeper Desktop local API, metadata only (who/frequency/recency/two-way), supporter-lane single chats, 2026-06-03. Method + caveats above. Data: `thoughts/shared/network-vibe-orbit.csv`.
- Community lane deliberately excluded from scoring (OCAP guardrail).
- Energy/lane *reads* are inferred judgement on the metadata, for founder confirmation — not measured.

## Relates to
- [[relationship-first-crm]] — the governing philosophy (belonging before money; artists, not heroes)
- [[ghl-crm-strategy-map]] — the belonging ladder + operating model
- [[ecosystem-value-exchange]] — supporter give/get + the community OCAP frame
- [[four-lanes]] — Voice / Flow / Ground / Grants; why commercial ≠ philanthropy
- [[empathy-ledger]] — sovereign showcase + the renewal engine
- Plan: `act-network-circle-action-stages` — the who/how execution, tracer-first and gated

pages.title: The Field
pages.excerpt: A field is what carries force between two bodies without them touching. That is relational energy — the pull between people across distance. The Field is ACT's living model of that energy: not a contact database, but a sense of where energy is warm and where it has gone slack, read each morning, so we can be deliberate about what we give and what we receive.
pages.content:
> A field is what carries force between two bodies without them touching. That is relational energy — the pull between people across distance. **The Field** is ACT's living model of that energy: not a contact database, but a sense of where energy is warm and where it has gone slack, read each morning, so we can be deliberate about what we give and what we receive.

You don't *work* The Field. You **read** it, then you **tend** it.

## What it is (and is not)
- It **is** a living map of ACT's relationships, kept honest by what actually happens — every email, every meeting, every call — and grounded in who people really are in the institutional landscape.
- It is **not** a CRM, a pipeline, or a funnel. Belonging comes before money. People are artists and allies, not leads. The community lane is never laddered, scored, or dripped.

## The two lanes (never one funnel)
- **The orbit** — the supporter lane. Energy *toward* ACT, held in mutual pull: warmth rings, with the hand-picked `circle:gsd-alliance` core. Read by warmth and evidence.
- **The constellation** — the community lane. Sovereign contributors (storytellers, elders). Measured by what ACT **owes back**, never by their use to us. The transcript owes-ledger lives here.
- **The line** between them is never crossed into a funnel. (See [[energy-orbit]] for the mechanics.)

**The Kristy rule — one person, many relationships.** Some people genuinely hold both lanes: Kristy Bloomfield is a Traditional Owner and storyteller (community) *and* runs Oonchiumpa, partners directly on Goods, and leads youth-justice work (a working peer). The model holds this by separating the person from the relationships: `lane:community` is a **floor of protections** (no tiers, no drips, owes honoured — always), not a box; **earned crossover** (real work, not newsletter subscriptions) means multi-project tags are *correct*; `circle:gsd-alliance` on a community person is **pure recognition** — it must never drag comms automation with it; and `role:` tags carry the multiplicity (`role:traditional-owner` + `role:storyteller` + `role:partner` can all be true; `role:funder` on a person is usually the org/person confusion — the org receives funds, the person is not your funder).

## Reciprocity — the heart of it
Every relationship is alive when energy flows both ways. So the unit The Field tracks is not "frequency of contact" but **energy given / energy received**: did this touch *give* energy (we helped them) or *receive* it (they helped us)? Read each morning, the question is simple — *where is energy flowing, where is it stuck, what do I give today, what's being given to me?*

## Tending — reading what each relationship needs
You tend relationships the way you tend crops: not all the same, each by what it actually needs.
- **Water** — attention and contact. A relationship dries out without it; *cooling* is the field telling you something needs water.
- **Sun** — to be seen. Recognition, attribution, a platform, their work showcased. Being seen energises; for the constellation, honouring the owes *is* the sun.
- **Nutrients** — the specific thing this one needs to grow: an introduction, capital, advice, a door. Diagnosed per person, never one-size.
- **Support / staking** — holding someone up through a hard season; vouching, defending.

And the discipline: **don't over-water.** Some relationships need space, not more contact; over-tending smothers, and that is the extraction the model refuses. CivicGraph shows the *soil* a person is rooted in (their org, their community); timing is *seasonal* — you plant and harvest when it's right. So the next move per person stops being "ask X" and becomes a diagnosis: *does this need water, sun, or a specific nutrient?*

## Leaving the Field — where our own energy comes from
You cannot tend from an empty well. A field worked without rest goes to seed, and a tender who only ever gives runs dry. So the second motion of The Field is **leaving it** — stepping out to learn new methods, to be scientific, to be *fed* by people instead of feeding them, to rest. This is not neglect; it is how the tending stays possible. You come back with new energy, new methods, new seed to plant.

This reframes the travel: the World Tour is ACT **leaving the field to gather energy and insight**, then returning to plant it. The Field should hold this rhythm honestly — including an honest read of *our own* energy (are Nick and Ben replenished, or running dry?), because a depleted tender is the first thing the field feels.

Received energy, then, comes from two places: from *within* the field (a reciprocal touch) and from *leaving* it (learning, people, rest). Both count. Both feed the giving.

## The four feeds (what keeps it alive)
The Field is only as true as what flows into it. Four streams, enriched overnight by the local model (qwen), reviewed by Ben/Nic by day:

1. **The corpus** — all act.place email (benjamin/nicholas/hi/accounts). Not just *how warm* each person is (dyadic), but **who's in the room together** (the thread/CC graph) — the *edges* that make this a network and not a scatter. Stays local; content never leaves; the community line holds.
2. **The institutional graph** — CivicGraph/GrantScope. Resolve every person to their entities, boards, and directorships, then to *who else sits there*. This gives **position** (where someone sits in the landscape) and **paths** (the warm route to a cold target is through whoever's already on their board), with the funder-discernment overlay (halo-wash vs community-controlled).
3. **Live capture** — every meeting, call, and WhatsApp. A voice memo or one line, structured into *who · energy given · energy received · what they need · next move*. Frictionless or it won't happen. This is the reciprocity ledger, per touch — the truest warmth signal there is.
4. **Intent** — what Nick & Ben are actually trying. The bets, the experiments, the travel (the World Tour is a structured insight-gathering campaign, not a holiday). The Field holds ACT's strategy enacted through relationships, and what each conversation taught us.

## Enrichment — how The Field learns about people (understand, never corner)
Every enrichment passes one test: *does knowing this help us **tend** them — give the right water, sun, or nutrient, and honour them — or does it help us **corner** them?* If the second, we don't do it. The Field enriches to understand, not to target. Three families:

1. **Structural — public record.** CivicGraph (orgs/boards/interlocks — the soil, built) · LinkedIn (role, history) · ASIC/ORIC/ACNC directorships · media/news · academic (ORCID/OpenAlex). Tools available + keyed: **Exa** (`person_identity_map` already carries `exa_enriched`), **Firecrawl**, **Tavily**, **Perplexity**.
2. **Behavioural — the signal we already generate.** Beeper/WhatsApp warmth · Gmail/calendar history · the reciprocity ledger from live capture. Truer than any scrape — it's real interaction.
3. **Reflective — the richest, and the most aligned.** Us, writing about a person: what they're trying to do in the world, what they care about, what they might need, what we admire. The act of writing it *is* tending.

**The person page** (`thoughts/shared/people/<name>.md`, built by `scripts/build-person-pages.mjs`) holds four layers: **Soil** (CivicGraph, auto) · **Web & work** (Tavily/Exa, auto) · **Understanding** (qwen draft — overnight, local, free) · **Reflection** (the human texture, by hand). Community lane is **excluded** from web-profiling — storytellers are honoured via the owes-ledger, never researched for leverage. The B2B enrichers (Apollo/Clearbit) are powerful but their *spirit* is extractive — use data, refuse the lead-scoring frame.

## The daily face
Open The Field each morning. It shows where energy is flowing and where it's stuck, who is **warm but unasked** (the latent gold), who is **cooling**, what ACT **owes**, and the day's moves — per project (what's needed → who we have → the gaps → the next move) and per person.

Current surfaces: `thoughts/shared/orbit-viz.html` (the shape) · `thoughts/shared/project-scope-board.html` (the decisions). Built read-only by `scripts/build-orbit-viz.mjs` and `scripts/build-scope-board.mjs`.

## Family & friends — the inner ground
Dunbar's inner layers aren't a marketing audience; they're mostly **family and close friends** — the people the energy budget exists to protect. They carry `role:family` / `role:friend`, sit in the inner rings by right (no tier needed, no earning), and are **never** placed in a comms funnel. The Field holds them so the morning read can tell the truth: if the inner 5 is going quiet, that's the first thing to tend.

## Vocabulary
- **Read the Field** — the morning practice (sense before act).
- **Tend** — the deliberate act of giving or receiving energy.
- **The orbit / the constellation / the line** — supporter lane / community lane / the boundary.
- **Warm · cooling · latent · owed** — the states a relationship can be in.
- **Energy given / received** — the reciprocity ledger.

## How it stays better over time
The local model proposes overnight (enrichment, classifications, who-to-reach drafts); Ben/Nic correct by day; each correction becomes a labelled example that sharpens the next night's proposals (few-shot now, fine-tune later). Night shift drafts; day shift decides. No external write happens without a human. See the night-shift/day-shift split in `~/.claude/rules/workflow.md`.

## Guardrails (carried from the orbit)
Community lane never energy-scored (OCAP). All GHL/EL/Notion writes are gated, day-shift, human-in-loop. `consent-check` before anything outward-facing. Targets resolved live, never from stale mirrors or pasted IDs.

pages.title: The Four Lanes
pages.excerpt: ACT's internal economy. How money earned through the work flows back to the soul, the founders, the debts, the growth, and the communities. The body the soul lives in.
pages.content:
> ACT's internal economy. How money earned through the work flows back to the soul, the founders, the debts, the growth, and the communities. The body the soul lives in.

This file lives downstream of [[soul|Soul]]. It exists because the soul has a body, and the body needs feeding.

This is a draft. Edit freely. The shape has to be right before the wiring is.

---

## The Premise

Most organisations that work in the space ACT works in struggle to pay the people doing the work. The founders survive on grants, then burn out, then leave. The work either dies with them, or is absorbed by the next generation of consultants who do not carry the soul.

ACT's economic model rejects that pattern. Custodianship over ownership only works if the custodians can keep showing up. That means money has to flow not just to the work, but to the people doing it, to the debts being cleared, to the projects being grown, and to the communities being served. All four. Not one at the expense of the others.

We named four lanes. Every dollar that moves through ACT lands in one of them.

---

## The Four Lanes

### To Us
Director wages. Distributions through Knight Family Trust and Marchesi Family Trust. Anything that lands in Ben's life or Nic's life, or the lives of the people they go home to.

This lane exists because two humans hold the soul. If they cannot keep showing up, the soul has nowhere to live.

### To Down
Debts paid. Old liabilities cleared. Receivables collected. ATO obligations met. The $507K in outstanding invoices we are still chasing.

This lane exists because an org that owes money cannot move freely. Clearing the past is what frees the future.

### To Grow
Reinvestment into A Curious Tractor Pty Ltd, Harvest Pty Ltd, and the projects each entity carries (ACT Farm runs as a program on land held in Nic's trust, not its own Pty). New equipment for the Goods workshop. Site costs at Witta. Engineering hours for Empathy Ledger. Travel to Mount Isa.

This lane exists because the work has to keep getting better. Growth here is not scale. It is depth.

### To Others
Donations to A Kind Tractor when it activates. Fellowship payments. Anchor partner support. Community grants out. The hospitality money that lands in someone else's pocket because they were on the table when we earned it.

This lane exists because ACT exists in service of communities. A dollar that never reaches a community has not done its job.

---

## The Entity Flow

Money does not move in a single ledger. It moves through entities, and the structure is part of how the soul holds across the work.

### A Curious Tractor Pty Ltd
ACN 697 347 676. Registered 24 April 2026. Owned 50/50 by Knight Family Trust and Marchesi Family Trust. Directors: Ben and Nic. Bank: NAB. Accountant: Standard Ledger.

This is the trade muscle. Service revenue, contracts (QBE Catalysing Impact is the first), grants that need a corporate trustee land here. From here, distributions flow to the trusts, and from the trusts to the founders. The dual-trust ownership is what makes To Us clean instead of awkward.

### Harvest Pty Ltd (forming)
Standalone P&L for The Harvest. Lease, cafe, garden, table, events, retreats. Earns its own revenue. Reinvests its own growth. Distributes back when it makes sense.

The reason Harvest gets its own entity is so its story is legible. We can see what The Harvest cost, what it earned, what it bought, and what it gave away, without it mashing into a single ACT ledger that makes none of it readable.

### ACT Farm (program, not a Pty)
ACT Farm runs as a program (code ACT-FM). The 150-acre Black Cockatoo Valley land is held in Nic's family trust and leased to ACT; conservation work, land practice, residencies and the BCV arc run on it. A Farm Pty Ltd only forms if and when the Farm earns enough to stand on its own P&L.

### A Kind Tractor Ltd
ACN 669 029 341. Company Limited by Guarantee. ACNC-registered. Currently dormant. Not yet DGR-endorsed.

When A Kind Tractor activates, it becomes the channel for tax-deductible donations and DGR-only philanthropic capital. It holds the public-good cap. Until activation, it sits ready.

### Sole trader (Nic's ABN 21 591 780 066)
The legacy entity. Trading migrates out of here into A Curious Tractor Pty Ltd by 30 June 2026. Pre-cutover invoices stay with the sole trader. After cutover, no new work runs through it.

---

## Why Separate Entities, Not One

Because each project earns the right to grow on its own revenue. The Harvest's money funds the Harvest's growth. A Curious Tractor Pty Ltd is the holding muscle that carries the founder relationship; ACT Farm runs as a program on trust-held land until it earns its own entity.

If we ran a single Pty Ltd with every project mashed into one ledger, the financial story would blur. To Grow at Harvest would be invisible. Founders would have no clean way to see whether each project pays its way.

The structure costs more in compliance. It saves more in legibility. Legibility is what makes the soul able to read its own body.

---

## LCAA in Money

Every dollar that moves through any ACT entity gets two tags: which project, and which Listen-Curiosity-Action-Art phase.

- **Listen** dollars: fieldwork, story collection, time spent on country, research with no deliverable yet.
- **Curiosity** dollars: prototypes, experiments, R&D, the engineering of things that have not been proven to work.
- **Action** dollars: delivery, services, operations, infrastructure, things shipping.
- **Art** dollars: artefacts, journals, public works, cultural production, the surface of the work.

A quarter's spend can be reported as: `Listen 28% / Curiosity 22% / Action 32% / Art 18%`. That ratio is the answer to "are we living the method, or just talking about it?"

When Listen drops below 20%, we have stopped sitting in rooms before we build. When Art drops below 10%, the work has gone quiet. When Action breaches 50%, we are scaling rather than seeding. The ratios are not rules. They are signals.

---

## Founder Sustainability is Method, Not Tax

The honest line, written into `soul.md` already: Ben and Nic have not paid each other enough this year. The entity is only just becoming the right shape. We can fix it. The weirdness of running something that pays everyone but its founders is real, and it lands.

This file exists partly so that line is taken seriously and not treated as a confession. Custodianship over ownership requires the custodians to keep showing up. A founder who cannot pay their mortgage cannot stay. A founder who burns out is not regenerative.

To Us is therefore not a tax on the work. It is part of the work. A dollar paid to Ben so he can be present with Carla, Pollyanna, and Jolie is the same kind of dollar as a fellowship paid to a community partner. A dollar paid to Nic so he can keep building places his parents recognise as his is the same kind of dollar as a donation to A Kind Tractor.

Both are how the soul keeps a body to live in.

---

## Beautiful Obsolescence Applied to Money

Same discipline as everything else ACT does. The point is not to build a financial empire. The point is to build a system that, if Ben and Nic stepped away, could still run.

That means:

- Standalone P&Ls so each project's economy is portable.
- Documentation good enough that someone else could read the books.
- Distributions structured so the founders are not the bottleneck.
- A charity arm ready to absorb the public-good elements when the time comes.

We are not building this to be inherited by family. We are building it to be handed back to the work itself.

---

## What This Looks Like in Practice

The four lanes show up in three places.

### Notion top card (daily)
A live snapshot of the current quarter. Updated weekly from Xero.

```
Q1 FY27 to date
  To Us      $X
  To Down    $Y
  To Grow    $Z
  To Others  $W

LCAA: Listen 28% · Curiosity 22% · Action 32% · Art 18%
Founders YTD: Ben $A · Nic $B
```

### Weekly digest (every Monday)
One line added to the existing digest:

> Lane most behind this week: To Us. Soul check: when did you last sit in a room with someone you did not have to convince of anything?

### Public translation (act.place/economy)
Not financials. Story told in money. A funder or community partner reads:

> Q4 To Grow funded the Goods pitch to Minderoo and the BG Fit fieldwork. Q4 To Others sent X to anchor partners. Q4 To Us paid the founders for the first time at the level the entity now allows.

The numbers do not need to be exact in public. The shape of the four lanes does.

---

## What This is Not

This is not a tax minimisation strategy. The structure is what the structure is because of how the work needs to be held, not because we optimised for tax.

This is not a financial transparency platform. CivicGraph does that for other people's public money. ACT's own transparency is for ACT's people first, and for our partners as a courtesy.

This is not a justification for under-paying anyone. It is the opposite. The lanes exist precisely so under-payment cannot hide.

---

## Backlinks

- [[soul|Soul]]: the source upstream of this file
- [[act-identity|ACT Identity]]: who ACT is, the body the soul inhabits
- [[lcaa-method|LCAA Method]]: the loop every dollar gets tagged against
- [[beautiful-obsolescence|Beautiful Obsolescence]]: the discipline applied to money
- [[../decisions/act-core-facts|ACT Core Facts]]: the canonical entity structure

pages.title: The Full Idea
pages.excerpt: A community-led infrastructure for youth justice in Australia. Three rings of work. Seven methods. Ten anchor communities. Three years to make it visible at scale.
pages.content:
> *A community-led infrastructure for youth justice in Australia. Three rings of work. Seven methods. Ten anchor communities. Three years to make it visible at scale.*

This document is the **complete idea**, in one place, written for walk-through review. Not a pitch to a specific funder. Not a deck. The whole architecture so it can be sat with, edited, and built from.

**How to use this document:** the headings below are the sections. Walk through them in order. At the end of each section there is an *Open questions* block — that is where to leave notes, corrections, and what should change. Each section is meant to be edited independently.

---

## §1 · What it is, in one paragraph

**STAY.** is a three-year program that leaves a library. Seven method books in **The STAY Series**, ten community volumes from ten anchor communities on Country, around fifty hand-stitched young-person Journals, and a national edition that goes to every electorate office in the country. The library is the proof — and it is the destination. A small team accompanies it into being by holding ten Indigenous-led communities over three years, wiring the infrastructure that makes their work legible (CivicGraph + ALMA-governed JusticeHub evidence + Empathy Ledger), and producing the artefacts the rest of the world will fly in to read.

The word **STAY** carries the whole methodology. *Stay where you are* — don't move children off Country to be punished. *Stay connected* — don't parachute in and leave. *Stay in the work* — don't file the artefact and forget. The library is the form all three meanings take.

> **Open questions §1**
> - "Ends in a library" — right verb? Or "becomes" / "leaves" / "produces"?
> - "The world will fly in to read" — strong enough this early in the doc, or save it for §7?
> - Ten communities locked? (Three Circles canon = ten; original Staying tier was seven)

---

## §2 · Why it exists

Australian youth justice has more reports, frameworks, evaluations, peak bodies, lived-experience panels, and government strategies than at any point in its history.

It also has more children in detention, more recidivism, and more lateral violence in the sector than at any point in recent memory.

**The problem is not absence of evidence.** It is that the evidence, the relationships, and the stories are all held in different rooms — and the rooms don't talk to each other.

- Frameworks live in consultancy decks.
- Stories live in unfunded community organisations.
- Funding flows live in spreadsheets nobody reads.
- Indigenous knowledge lives where it has always lived — in Country, in Elders, in Tuesday afternoon check-ins that no funder has ever counted as governance.

The cost of detaining one Australian child for one year: **$1.33M** *(ROGS 2024–25)*.
The projected detention rate for Aboriginal & Torres Strait Islander children by 2030–31: **24.6 per 10,000** *(Closing the Gap)*.

We are not here to argue these numbers. We are here to **answer** them.

> **Open questions §2**
> - Is the cost figure right ($1.33M)? Should we use the 3-year figure ($3.9M) instead?
> - Anything missing from the "different rooms" framing?

---

## §3 · What is already built

This program is **not starting from zero.** The infrastructure layer is already shipping:

| Layer                                     | What it is                                                                                     |                                                                                                         Live numbers |
| ----------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------: |
| **CivicGraph**                            | The legibility layer — entities, relationships, place-mapping, daily syncs from public sources |       **100,036** entities · **199,001** relationships · **94.1%** entity-match accuracy · **96%** postcode coverage |
| **ALMA-governed JusticeHub evidence** | The case library of community-led models that already work                                     | **1,775** community models, of which **128** are verified at the top three tiers (Indigenous-led, Effective, Proven) |
| **JusticeHub**                            | The public-facing front end — search, dossiers, MCP agent tools, place pages                   |                                                                       Live at justicehub.com.au · 6 live agent tools |
| **Empathy Ledger**                        | Consent and sovereignty layer — every voice transcript, every story, every consent             |                                                         **226** storytellers · OCAP/CARE protocols at the data layer |
| **CONTAINED**                             | The companion exhibition — a shipping container on the road, currently at Mounty Yarns         |                                                                                                          Active tour |
| **Justice funding tracking**              | Indexed records of grants, contracts, donations, procurement                                   |                              **52K** justice funding records · **672K** AusTender contracts · **312K** AEC donations |

The full stack: **CivicGraph + ALMA-governed evidence + JusticeHub + Empathy Ledger + CONTAINED.**

This is the answer to *"how do you know it works?"* — built so communities can witness, document, verify, and publish what already works on their own terms.

> **Open questions §3**
> - Are these the right numbers to lead with?
> - Anything missing? Should EL v2 or the bot integrations be on this list?

---

## §4 · The seven models

These are the seven methods the program runs on. Each one has its own page in the journal: cover on the left, explanation on the right. Here they are in journal order with the locked copy and the diagram.

---

### §4.1 · The Three Circles

![](../output/three-circles-journal-spread.png)

**Subtitle:** *A community-led methodology for working with people the system has failed.*

**The model:**

| # | Circle | Who | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **The Edge** | The people the system has failed hardest. | First. Always. |
| 2 | **The Next** | The kin, workers, advocates immediately around them. | Second. Strengthened by what comes from the centre. |
| 3 | **The Rest** | Funders, government, sector. | Last. Changed by what travels outward. |

**Tagline:** *start at the edge. work outward.*

> *"Authority sits with the people closest to the consequence."* — Tyson Yunkaporta, after 65,000 years.
>
> Documented again by Elinor Ostrom across five continents. Proven at national scale by Fundación Diagrama in Spain over thirty years.
>
> The Three Circles is the methodology: start where the system has failed hardest, and let the work travel outward. Most programs do the opposite. Most programs fail.

> **Open questions §4.1**
> - Does the diagram land?
> - Anything in the back-blurb that needs softening or sharpening?

---

### §4.2 · The Living Map Loop

![](../output/alma-loop-journal.png)

**Subtitle:** *How communities grow the ALMA-governed evidence commons.*

**The four moves:**

| # | Step | What happens | Who does it |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **WITNESS** | Someone notices a working model the formal system has never recognised. | A community member, a worker, anyone willing to look. |
| 2 | **DOCUMENT** | The model gets captured properly — story, mechanism, conditions, outcomes — in the witness's own voice. | Storyteller + the person running the model. |
| 3 | **VERIFY** | Community sovereignty over what counts as proof. Elder-, kin-, place-led validation. **Not** academic peer review. **Not** government audit. | The community itself, on its own terms. |
| 4 | **PUBLISH** | The entry joins the Map. Now searchable, citable, fundable. | The Map (the infrastructure does the rest). |

**Tagline:** *the things that work are already happening. we just have to write them down — properly.*

> 1,775 community-led models, and growing.
> 128 already verified by Elders, communities, or trials.
> The rest are the work — and the Loop is how we move them up the ladder.
>
> The system doesn't know what works because it never asked. The ALMA-governed evidence commons is the answer to that — built so communities can witness, document, verify and publish *what already works*, on their own terms.
>
> Every entry attracts the next witness. The library grows by recognition, not by extraction.

> **Open questions §4.2**
> - Is the WITNESS / DOCUMENT / VERIFY / PUBLISH naming right?
> - 1,775 / 128 — confirm or update.

---

### §4.3 · Three Ripples

![](../output/three-ripples-journal-spread.png)

**Subtitle:** *The infrastructure that makes the edge legible to capital.*

**The rings:**

| Ring | Name | What it actually is | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **The Edge** | Country, kin, the relationship | Maranguka 23%↓ violent crime · Oonchiumpa 95% diversion |
| 2 | **The World Model** *(CivicGraph)* | The legibility layer the hierarchy refused to build | 100,036 entities · 199,001 relationships · 94.1% match accuracy |
| 3 | **Funding That Finds You** | Capital that follows verified outcomes | 672K contracts indexed · 312K donations · 52K justice funding records |
| 4 *(dashed)* | *the state, eventually* | The hierarchy catches up last | — |

**The two horizons of Ring 3:**

| | **TODAY — the familiar rail** | **TOMORROW — the new rail** |
|---|---|---|
| What it is | Grants and contracts already in use — but routed by the world model so they actually land at the edge | Capital that follows verified outcomes without going through the hierarchy |
| What changes | Same instrument. Different routing. | The instrument itself changes. |
| Examples | Targeted grants, justice reinvestment, place-based contracts | Hypercerts, ImpactQF, outcomes contracts |

> 100,036 entities. 199,001 relationships. 94.1% match accuracy.
>
> The legibility layer the hierarchy refused to build — wired so capital can find the edge two ways: the way you already know, and the way you didn't know was possible yet.
>
> *Funding that finds you, instead of you having to find it.*

> **Open questions §4.3**
> - Hypercerts + ImpactQF — still the right naming or has it shifted?
> - Are CivicGraph numbers OK on the cover?

---

### §4.4 · I Have · I Am · I Can

![](../output/intentionality-canvas-journal-spread.png)

**Subtitle:** *Nine resources every child draws on to face adversity.*

**The nine resources:**

| | Category | What it is | Three items |
|---|---|---|---|
| **I HAVE** | external supports — what's around me | trusting, loving relationships · role models who show what resilient looks like · people who set limits with care |
| **I AM** | inner strengths — what I carry | respectful of myself · confident and optimistic · empathic and caring of others |
| **I CAN** | skills — what I do | solve problems · stay with a task / persevere · reach out for help when I need it |

**Tagline:** *resilience is contagious. its absence is also contagious.*

> Edith Grotberg studied street children in Lima — kids who'd lived on the streets for months or years, who'd used drugs, who'd been beaten by police, who'd sold sex for food. And she found the same thing she'd found in twenty other countries: the kids who *made it* drew on three pools of resources.
>
> **I have.** External supports — trusting relationships, role models, people who held the line.
> **I am.** Inner strengths — self-respect, confidence, empathy.
> **I can.** Skills — problem-solving, perseverance, knowing when to ask for help.
>
> Most programs design for the visible deficit. The resilience research says: design for the nine.
>
> And the hardest finding from Lima — from the families displaced by political violence: *resilience is contagious. Its absence is also contagious.* When the parents fled into trauma, the children fell with them. When the parents engaged the new world, the children rose with them. Whatever you build for a child, build the same thing for the adults around the child — or the child has no model to copy.
>
> *— after Edith Henderson Grotberg, Resilience in Street Children and in Victims of Political Violence in Peru, Lima 2006.*

> **Open questions §4.4**
> - The nine items — keep as-is or swap any?
> - JusticeHub logo placeholder — which logo file should be composited in?

---

### §4.5 · The Field Canvas

![](../output/field-diagnostic-journal-spread.png)

**Subtitle:** *Look honestly at the whole field — above the soil and below — before you change anything.*

**The 5 P scan:**

| Domain | What you read | Hidden pattern |
|---|---|---|
| **Projects** | What's active. What's earning. What's stalled. | Where money comes from vs where energy goes. |
| **People** | Who's here. Who's paid. Who decides. | The unspoken pay gap. The implicit operating agreement. |
| **Pulses** | Operating rhythm. Weekly / monthly / quarterly. | Whether urgency is driving priority instead of strategy. |
| **Process** | How work moves through. Closure rate. | Starting is easy, finishing is hard. WIP creep. |
| **Products** | What's packaged. What's priced. Go-to-market. | "If we build it well enough, they'll come" — they don't. |

**The PTO discipline:** *the tractor powers one implement at a time.*

| Lane | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Drive** | Connect the PTO now. Maximum 3 projects. |
| **Field** | Planted. Not powered yet. Hold the line. |
| 🔧 **Shed** | Park, sunset, or hand over. |

**The 90-day Furrow Plan** — six tracks every diagnostic ends in: Mission, Revenue, People, Product, Partnerships, Rhythm. Each one with an action verb, a target, and the proof it landed.

**Tagline:** *what grows above is a function of the soil below.*

> Most strategic plans fail because they describe the field above the ground and ignore the soil below. The Field Canvas is the tool that makes you look at both.
>
> Above: revenue, platforms, community, proof — the things outsiders see. Below: culture, operations, market — the soil that's either growing the visible work or rotting it. And under that, the root system: the infrastructure, relationships, philosophy and financial spine that connect everything.

> **Open questions §4.5**
> - Is the outback eucalyptus visual the right metaphor or does it need to change?
> - The 5 P spine — lock or change one?

---

### §4.6 · Listen · Curiosity · Action · Art

![](../output/lcaa-loop-journal.png)

**Subtitle:** *A Curious Tractor's operating system. Four phases. One loop.*

**The four phases:**

| # | Phase | What you do | The discipline |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Listen** | Receive what's already there. Country, Traditional Owners, Community, Elders, Youth, the Silenced. | **Don't arrive with solutions.** |
| 2 | **Curiosity** | Follow the threads. *What if? Who says it has to be this way?* | **Resist premature closure.** |
| 3 | **Action** | Build, prototype, test, iterate. Co-creation. Ship early. Document for handover. | **If you can't hand it over, you're still in Curiosity.** |
| 4 | **Art** | The work made beautiful, meaningful, lasting. | **Art is how we know we've learned something.** |

**Tagline:** *art returns us to listen. the cycle continues.*

> *If you can't hand it over, you're still in Curiosity.*
>
> Most methodologies are checklists. Listen, Curiosity, Action, Art is a loop — and the loop never closes.
>
> The journal you are holding is art. The CONTAINED tour is art. This story is art. They will all return us to Listen.

> **Open questions §4.6**
> - Drop the acronym entirely on covers? (current rule says yes)
> - Keep all four discipline lines on the right page or trim?

---

### §4.7 · Fire Crescendo

![](../output/fire-crescendo-journal.png)

**Subtitle:** *On building things slowly. Year 1 to Year 3.*

**The six stages × three years:**

| # | Stage | Year | What's happening |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Ember | Y1 | A single relationship. One Elder. One yarn. |
| 2 | Tinder | Y1 | Trust. Showing up when you said you would. |
| 3 | Kindling | Y2 | Small structured work. The first camp. The first cohort. |
| 4 | Campfire | Y2 | Communities visit each other. Storytellers tell their own stories. |
| 5 | Roaring fire | Y3 | The work spreads. Other communities ask how. |
| 6 | Bonfire | Y3 | Holding warmth for people who weren't there at the start. |

**Tagline:** *fire does not arrive at bonfire stage. you build it, slowly, with attention.*

> Most programs fail because someone tries to light the bonfire in Year 1. Funders ask for bonfire-shaped outcomes from ember-stage work. Boards demand scale before the kindling has even caught.
>
> Fire Crescendo is the diagram that gives funders the language to fund Year 1 properly — and gives the team the language to say *"no, not yet."*

> **Open questions §4.7**
> - CAMPFIRE worked example (Brodie Germaine, Mount Isa) — separate page after this one. Confirmed.
> - Six stages or three?

---

## §5 · The proposition

A three-year program shaped as three movements. The movements come from Listen · Curiosity · Action · Art compressed into the program's whole arc:

| Year | Name | Where | What happens |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Year 1** | *Listen* | The ten anchor communities, in Australia | Heavy in-community engagement. Relationships. The first round of journals begins. The infrastructure layer (CivicGraph + Living Map + Empathy Ledger) is wired to the field arm so every story has a home. |
| **Year 2** | *Compare* | Distributed European exchange | Each community sends a young person + a support person to **one** European destination — Diagrama (Spain), Halt (Holland), or the Children's Hearings system (Scotland). Reciprocal European visits to Australia in the same year. Brings the international peer relationship into the journal. |
| **Year 3** | *Tell* | Back to the ten communities, then outward | Ten community-led launches in the ten places. A published book gathers the ten journals into a single national volume. The work goes home before it goes to the city. |

Three acts. Listen / Compare / Tell. Funders, audiences, and books all need three acts.

> **Open questions §5**
> - Ten or seven communities? (Three Circles canon = ten; Staying tier = seven)
> - Is the "Compare" frame for Year 2 right, or should it be "Curiosity"?

---

## §6 · The ten anchor communities

Final selection through assertive in-community visits — the only verification that works. There is no funnel. We start with the people we already know and trust, then radiate outward through trust, recommendation, and openness. **The filter is relationship, not process.**

| State | Likely candidate | Status |
|---|---|---|
| **NT** | Oonchiumpa (Mparntwe) — Aunty Bev, Tanya Turner, Kristy Bloomfield | Existing partnership ✓ |
| **QLD (north)** | PICC (Palm Island) — Richard Cassidy, Bwgcolman families | Existing partnership ✓ |
| **QLD (Mount Isa)** | CAMPFIRE — Brodie Germaine | Existing partnership ✓ |
| **QLD (Brisbane region)** | EPIC Pathways / MMEIZC (Stradbroke) / Toowoomba — three-way pick | Open |
| **NSW** | Maranguka (Bourke Tribal Council) | Need to approach |
| **NSW** | Mounty Yarns (Mt Druitt) | Existing relationship |
| **WA** | Olabud Doogethu (Halls Creek) | Need to approach |
| **TAS** | Prevention Not Detention (Loic Fery's coalition) | Pipeline contact |
| **VIC** | OPEN | — |
| **SA** | OPEN | — |

**This is not 10 grants. It is 10 long-term relationships** the centre learns from, the international tour celebrates, and the artefact in Year 3 is built around.

**Cultural protocol — non-negotiable:**

1. No community is approached without prior consultation with existing ACT relationships in that region.
2. Elder and Council sign-off before any photographs, recordings, or journals begin.
3. OCAP/CARE protocols at the data layer via Empathy Ledger — the legal and technical baseline, not aspirational.
4. Young person owns their journal. Right of withdrawal at any point.
5. Subjects under 18 require guardian and cultural authority sign-off.
6. Cultural review fees are budgeted as line items, not absorbed as goodwill labour.
7. No exhibition opens without at least one young person or cultural representative present.
8. Income from book/exhibition sales flows on a published transparent split to subjects and their nominated community organisations.

> **Open questions §6**
> - VIC + SA candidates — how do we source them?
> - Should CAMPFIRE be its own slot or counted under QLD-north?

---

## §7 · The Library — *The STAY Series*

> *At the end of this program we have a library. Not a report. A library.*

Imagine a shelf. Aged cream spines, hand-set serif type, soft wear at the corners. Seven slim Penguin Modern Classics-style paperbacks lined up — **The STAY Series, No. 01 through No. 07** — and leaning against them at the end of the row, a stack of hand-stitched young-person Journals. Behind the shelf, ten community volumes. In front of the shelf, an open invitation: *come here to learn.*

This is the move that takes the program from **framework to action**, from *thinking about the work* to *the work itself in your hands*.

![](../output/the-library-shelf.png)

### What's on the shelf

#### The STAY Series — the seven method books

| No. | Title | Subtitle |
|---:|---|---|
| **01** | THE THREE CIRCLES | *Start at the edge. Work outward.* |
| **02** | THE LIVING MAP LOOP | *1,775 community models, and growing.* |
| **03** | THREE RIPPLES | *The infrastructure of the edge.* |
| **04** | I HAVE · I AM · I CAN | *Nine resources for resilience.* |
| **05** | THE FIELD CANVAS | *Look at the whole field. Above and below.* |
| **06** | LISTEN · CURIOSITY · ACTION · ART | *Four phases. One loop.* |
| **07** | FIRE CRESCENDO | *On building things slowly.* |

The series mark on every spine: **`THE STAY SERIES · NO. 01`** through **`NO. 07`**. Same paper, same serif, same roundel position, same photography setup. They read as a series the moment Lucy — or anyone — sees them on a shelf.

#### The other layers of the library

| Layer | What it is | How many |
|---|---|---|
| **Young-person Journals** | Bound book per young person — A5, hand-stitched, ~80–120 pages. Portraits, handwriting, voice transcripts, letters from Aunties and uncles, ledger entries of who showed up and when, the European exchange visit as its own chapter. | ~50 — one per young person across the ten communities |
| **Community volumes** | One bound volume per community — collected work, place, voices, photographs, the model running in real life. | 10 — one per anchor community |
| **Travel Diaries** *(bidirectional — see §7.5)* | The same notebook a young person from Mparntwe takes to Murcia, and the same notebook an Olga from Diagrama takes to Mount Isa. The diary that becomes the meeting place. | One per visiting cohort, both directions |
| **The national edition** | A single printed volume gathering the ten community volumes (with consent) into one national artefact. | 1 — every electorate office gets a copy |

**Owned by the young people.** Not ACT. Not the funder. OCAP/CARE protocols at the data layer through Empathy Ledger. Right of withdrawal at any point. Income from sales flows on a published transparent split to subjects and their nominated community organisations.

### What the library *does*

The shelf is not the end. It is the **beginning of the second program** — the one that runs when the books exist:

1. **People can read the work.** A magistrate in Hobart, a Minister in Canberra, an Aunty in Halls Creek, a youth worker in Birmingham — the methodology is now a thing they can hold, not a deck they have to sit through.
2. **People can buy the work.** The books go to bookshops, libraries, schools. The royalties flow back to communities and young people on a published split.
3. **People can come to the work.** The library becomes a tour: visitors fly into Australia to learn the methods *in the places they were built*. Mount Isa, Mparntwe, Palm Island, Halls Creek. Indigenous-led learning. The kind of civic-tech tourism Spain has been doing for thirty years through Diagrama — but here, on Country, with the people who built it.
4. **Young people can teach the work.** The young people whose journals are on the shelf become **the teachers**. They show their books. They walk visitors through their journey. They explain the methods in their own words. *The library makes them publishers and hosts, not subjects.*
5. **Other communities can write their own books.** The seven methods are forkable. The journal template is forkable. A community in Birmingham, in Lima, in Murcia, in Christchurch can pick up the series and add their own volumes — and the library grows.

### The macro reframe

This is what moves Australia from a country that **imports** youth justice frameworks to a country that **exports** them. From the place that has the highest Indigenous incarceration rate in the OECD to the place the rest of the world flies in to learn from.

> *Indigenous thinking. World model. Visitors invited in. Australia as the world-leading community model.*
>
> The library is not the report. The library is the proof — and the destination.

### The components, in detail

**The seven method books.** The Penguin-style series. Already designed. Live in `wiki/output/`. Each one has its own page in the journal (covers in §4 of this document). They are the *first run of the press.*

**The young-person Journals.** Year 3 delivery. Hand-stitched. The visual register is the **ledger page** — Christian Boltanski, Sophie Calle, Edmund Clark, Theaster Gates, Anselm Kiefer, Judy Watson, Daniel Boyd, Vernon Ah Kee, Tony Albert, Brook Andrew. Hand-made, lived-in, accumulated over time, the young person at the centre. See `tools/three-ripples-ledger.html` for the visual mockup.

**The community volumes.** One per anchor community, accumulating across all three years. Bound at the end of Year 3 alongside each community-led launch.

**The national edition.** The one volume that gathers the ten community volumes into a single national artefact. Sent to every electorate office. Sold publicly. The thing on the shelf in the public library.

**The companion exhibition (CONTAINED).** The shipping container on the road. Travels alongside the launches. The library you walk *into.*

**The platform underneath (CivicGraph + Living Map + JusticeHub + Empathy Ledger).** The infrastructure side of the library. Every voice in a journal traces back to a CivicGraph entity. Every model in a method book is verified through the Living Map. The library has receipts.

> **Open questions §7**
> - "The STAY Series" naming — locked.
> - The shelf as hero image — three variants generating in parallel. Pick one.
> - The "young people as teachers" frame — keep gentle (current) or sharper ("the publishers, not the subjects")?
> - Royalty split — who decides the percentages? When?
> - **TODO:** the seven covers themselves currently have no series mark on the spine. Next round of cover re-spins should bake in **`THE STAY SERIES · NO. 01`** through **`NO. 07`** on the spine and bottom of front cover.

---

## §7.5 · The Travel Diary — *bidirectional, by design*

> *The same notebook a young person from Mparntwe takes to Murcia. The same notebook an Olga from Diagrama takes to Mount Isa.*

The Travel Diary is the meeting place. One physical object, one template, used in both directions. When the diary is on a desk in Spain it is the record of a young person from Country in Europe. When the diary is on a desk in Halls Creek it is the record of a European visitor learning at the source. The same notebook holds both.

This is the format that **operationalises *Australia as destination***. It's the artefact funders, magistrates, and the international civic-tech world walk away with — the proof that the traffic now flows both ways.

### The format

| | What's in it |
|---|---|
| **Cover** | Aged kraft, hand-stitched, with a small linocut symbol of the journey direction (an arrow, a plane, two sets of footprints) |
| **First spread** | Who is travelling, who is hosting, the dates, the Country at each end |
| **Daily entries** | Hand-written by the traveller. Photographs taped in. Receipts. Tickets. Pressed leaves. Notes on what was unexpected. Names of the people who held the room. |
| **The interview** | One long conversation with the host community, in their words. Voice transcript via Empathy Ledger sits alongside the handwritten version. |
| **The model encounter** | Which of the seven STAY Series methods showed up here? In what form? What did it look like in this place that it doesn't look like at home? |
| **What I'm taking back** | The traveller's own words on what they will carry home. |
| **What I'm leaving here** | A page the traveller writes for the host. Stays in the host's diary. |

### How it runs (bidirectional)

| Direction | Who travels | Who hosts | What gets made |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Outbound** *(AU → Europe)* | A young person + a support person from each of the ten anchor communities | Diagrama (Spain), Halt (Holland), Children's Hearings (Scotland) | Ten outbound diaries — one per community pairing |
| **Inbound** *(Europe → AU)* | Small delegations from each European host | The ten anchor communities, hosting on Country | Three inbound diaries — one per European delegation |

**Total: ~13 Travel Diaries per cycle.** Each one becomes a chapter in the relevant young-person Journal *and* a standalone publication that joins the library.

### Why this matters

It collapses the centre-and-periphery framing every philanthropic conversation about Indigenous justice gets stuck in. Spain has been receiving international visitors for thirty years through Diagrama. The Travel Diary is the move that turns Australia into the **other end** of that exchange — not the place that sends people away to learn, but the place people come *to.*

The diary makes the reciprocity legible in a way a report cannot. Two notebooks, sitting next to each other on the library shelf, one Australian and one Spanish — both filled out by the same kind of hand, both in the same template — is the entire argument made physical.

> *The traffic flows both ways. The proof is on the desk.*

> **Open questions §7.5**
> - Format — kraft hand-stitched (current) or aged-cream Penguin-style to match the STAY Series?
> - Naming — "Travel Diary" (current) or "Field Notebook" or "Crossing"?
> - Should the inbound diaries be one per delegation (3) or one per community-host pairing (10)?
> - Does the diary need its own numbering inside the STAY Series — e.g. "NO. 08–20" — or is it a separate sub-series called "STAY · Crossings"?

---

## §8 · The team and cadence

**Lean by design.** Two people, not twenty.

- **1 FTE lead + 1 support person** — the core team that rotates through the ten communities
- **4 months on / 8 months off** rhythm — heavy in-community engagement when present, processing and journal production when home
- **One community close to Brisbane** for cheap, frequent low-friction visits and a shorter feedback loop
- **Cultural review fees and Elder governance** budgeted as line items, not absorbed as goodwill labour
- **The infrastructure layer** (CivicGraph, Living Map, Empathy Ledger, JusticeHub) is maintained by the existing ACT engineering team — not a new hire

This is the smallest possible team that can hold ten communities with depth. Anything bigger overwhelms a community when it arrives. Anything smaller can't sustain the cadence.

> **Open questions §8**
> - 1+1 vs 2+1? (current draft = 1+1)
> - 4/8 vs 6/6? (current draft = 4/8)

---

## §9 · The ask (in three tiers)

> *Fire does not arrive at bonfire stage. You build it, slowly, with attention.* — Model 07

The three tiers borrow the language of **Fire Crescendo** — the seventh book in the STAY Series — because the budget tells the same story as the methodology. A funder picks where they want to enter the fire.

| | **🔥 Foundation** | **🔥🔥 Crescendo** | **🔥🔥🔥 Bonfire** |
|---|---|---|---|
| **3-year total** | ~$1.8M | **~$3.43M** | ~$6.0M |
| **Annual flow** | ~$600K/year | ~$1.0M / $1.24M / $1.20M | ~$2.0M/year |
| **Communities** | 5 anchor | **10 anchor** | 10 + annual national gathering |
| **Team** | 1 FTE lead | 1 FTE + 1 support | 2 FTE + 1 support |
| **Cadence** | 3 months on / 9 off | 4 / 8 | 6 / 6 |
| **Year 2 — international exchange** | Deferred — one small scoping trip | Distributed exchange, ~14 travellers (Spain · Holland · Scotland) | Full exchange + reciprocal AU visits + a full cohort week per host country |
| **The library — young-person Journals** | Year 3 only, simple binding | Year 3 only, hand-stitched + 1 archive | Three chapter deliveries (Y1 / Y2 / Y3), premium binding |
| **The library — community volumes** | 5 | **10** | 10 + slipcase boxed sets in every State Library |
| **The library — national edition** | — | 1 printed volume to every electorate office | 1 printed volume + national gallery tour (NGA / MCA / NGV / regional) |
| **Versus detaining 1 child for 3 years** *($3.9M)* | 46% of cost | **88% of cost** | 154% of cost |

**Crescendo is the default.** It is the shape that *moves*: small enough to fund without negotiation, big enough to do the work, structured so every line earns its place — and big enough that the library at the end is the real artefact, not a deliverable.

For context, the line that should never need to be defended in a funder meeting:

> Detaining one Australian child for three years costs $3.9M. **The Crescendo tier runs the entire program for less than that** — across ten Indigenous-led communities, sending fourteen people to Europe and bringing Europe back, and producing the seven-book STAY Series + ten community volumes + ~50 young-person journals + the national edition.

> **Open questions §9**
> - Tier names: **Foundation / Crescendo / Bonfire** — locked. Foundation is what Year 1 lays for the fire to build on; Crescendo is when it catches; Bonfire is when it's undeniable. The budget tells the same story as Model 07.
> - Move the *"vs detaining one child"* line up to §2 as well, or keep it here?
> - Communities at the Crescendo tier: locked at 10 to match Three Circles canon.

---

## §10 · The lineage

This idea is not new. It is the synthesis of four lines of evidence that have all been on the table for a long time:

| Voice | Lineage | Contribution |
|---|---|---|
| **Tyson Yunkaporta** *(Sand Talk, 2019)* | Apalech (Wik), Nungar, Lost Mob | Aboriginal thinking is a structural refusal of hierarchy. Songlines as a working world model that has run for 65,000 years. **Authority sits with the people closest to the consequence.** |
| **Elinor Ostrom** *(Governing the Commons, 1990; Nobel 2009)* | Decades of fieldwork in Nepal, Maine, Spain, Swiss alps | Distributed governance *outperforms* hierarchy where authority sits with the people closest to the consequence and they can see each other's solutions. |
| **Fundación Diagrama** *(Spain, 30+ centres, 30 years)* | National-scale community-based youth justice | 20–30% reoffending vs Australia's 85%. Government-funded, community-run. The proof that this scales. |
| **Edith Henderson Grotberg** *(Resilience in Street Children and Victims of Political Violence in Peru, 2006)* | International resilience research | The I HAVE / I AM / I CAN framework. *Resilience is contagious. Its absence is also contagious.* |
| **Jack Dorsey / Block** *(From Hierarchy to Intelligence, 2026)* | Contemporary tech footnote | "Even fintech caught up." Capabilities + world model + intelligence layer + people at the edge. **Demoted from headline because the pattern is older than Block.** |

**The argument in one sentence:**

> Authority-at-the-edge is not new — Yunkaporta has been documenting it on this continent for thirty years, Ostrom proved it across five, Diagrama has been scaling it in Spain for thirty more, and Grotberg verified it in twenty countries with street children. What was always missing was the legibility infrastructure — the layer that lets capital, magistrates and the public see the work without going through the hierarchy. **We finally built it. It's called CivicGraph. The library on the next page is the proof.**

> **Open questions §10**
> - Lock the order: Yunkaporta first (place of standing), Dorsey demoted to footnote.
> - Add Maranguka and Oonchiumpa as Australian proof points alongside Diagrama?
> - The closing line — *"the library on the next page is the proof"* — does this assume the library spread is physically next? In the journal it is. In a slide deck it might not be. Worth a sharper version that travels.

---

## §11 · What's next

This document is the **starting point for review**, not the final shape. The walk-through process:

1. **Read each section in order.** The h2 headings are the navigation in Obsidian's outline pane.
2. **Edit each "Open questions" block** with notes, corrections, things to change.
3. **Tell me which sections need iteration first.** I'll work through them one at a time.

**Sections most likely to need iteration:**

- §5 (proposition) — depends on whether we go with 7 or 10 communities
- §6 (the ten) — VIC and SA candidates still open
- §9 (the ask) — tier names and the headline number
- §10 (the lineage) — the "argument in one sentence" is the most quotable line in the whole doc, worth getting exactly right

**Sections most likely to be already locked:**

- §3 (what is built) — the numbers are from the live database, current as of 2026-04-08
- §4 (the seven models) — locked in `thoughts/shared/handoffs/staying/models-locked.md`

---

## LCAA Phase

In the [[lcaa-method|LCAA Method]], The Full Idea is the architecture document for **STAY** — the program that operationalises LCAA across three years and ten communities to leave a library. The arc is the program's three-act structure (Listen / Compare / Tell) extended to the full LCAA frame, with the artefacts (seven method books, ten community volumes, ~50 hand-stitched young-person Journals, the national edition) as the durable Art layer.

LCAA arc for The Full Idea / STAY:
- **Listen — Year 1** — small team rotates through ten Indigenous-led anchor communities; deep accompaniment without arrival-and-departure; the team that *stays* through the season the program is ostensibly about
- **Curiosity — Year 2 European exchange** — distributed travel to [[diagrama|Diagrama]] (Spain), Halt (Holland), and the Children's Hearings system (Scotland); each anchor community sends a focused pair, comes home with a chapter; reciprocal European visits to Australia in the same year
- **Action — Year 3 community-led launches** — ten launches in ten places; The STAY Series (seven method books) + ten community volumes published; a national edition delivered to every electorate office
- **Art** — the per-young-person Journals as the centre artefact; the library itself as the proof; the artefacts the rest of the world flies in to read

STAY's bet: in a sector with more reports, frameworks, and panels than ever — and more children in detention than ever — the missing infrastructure is *holding*, not scaling. The library is the form that holds.

## Source documents

- `thoughts/shared/handoffs/staying/models-locked.md` — locked copy for all 7 models
- `thoughts/shared/handoffs/staying/visual-language.md` — visual language brief (Mode A covers + Mode B journal pages)
- `wiki/projects/staying.md` — original Staying program draft (2026-04-08, since reframed)
- `wiki/synthesis/the-edge-is-where-the-healing-is...md` — the synthesis underneath everything
- `wiki/concepts/lcaa-method.md` — canonical LCAA document
- `wiki/raw/2025-10-11-article-from-trouble-to-transformation-the-campfire-journey.md` — Brodie Germaine + CAMPFIRE
